name: Bo to Trang Bang
summary: Young beef from Trảng Bàng, the plate the provincial tourism center describes as thin slices, steamed or boiled, rolled in bánh tráng phơi sương with herbs and forest leaves. The same article names seven other beef plates and does not describe them. The article marks this as lunch. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Trảng Bàng, in phường Trảng Bàng, phường An Tịnh, and along Quốc lộ 22.
texture: The center says the beef is naturally sweet, the meat soft, the skin crisp. It says long-running kitchens choose animals of about 5 to 6 months, about 50 to 60 kg, for small fibers, little fat, and that sweetness. Those figures are that article's only ones.
taste: The roll the article describes is thin slices of steamed or boiled young beef, bánh tráng phơi sương, fresh rice noodles, garden herbs, and forest leaves: quế vị, lá cách, đọt cóc, sao nhái, and cải trời. Dip in mắm nêm or mixed fish sauce.
howToEat: Roll the beef in the Trảng Bàng sheet. The center says this steamed or boiled roll is the plate many visitors choose.

The same article also names bò nướng mọi, bò nướng sả, bò hấp gừng, bò nhúng giấm, bò nhúng mắm ruốc, lẩu đuôi bò, and cháo bò, plus offal plates it does not name. Those plates are separate dishes. This article does not describe their fire or their sauce.
The article marks bò tơ as lunch. A clock was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival. A price is Check on arrival.
where: Phường Trảng Bàng, phường An Tịnh, and along Quốc lộ 22.
seoTitle: Bo to Trang Bang — young beef and rice paper
seoDescription: Young beef of about 5 to 6 months, rolled in Trảng Bàng rice paper with forest leaves. The article marks it as lunch. A price is Check on arrival.
